description: int16 depth buffer keyed on float-bit-pattern (uint16 sw_depth, sw_depth_key() per pixel in all inner loops + SW_PutPixel)

asi.hypothesis: halve z traffic + replace FPU compare with int compare
asi.mechanism_learning: DOSBox has no cache/bus model: memory WIDTH is free; only INSTRUCTION COUNT matters. FPU compare ~= the extra int ops for key extraction (memcpy+shr), so net +insns per px. Future memory-size or FPU-avoidance ideas must be re-priced as pure instruction-count deltas.
asi.next: attack instruction count directly: flex backface cull (drop ~40% of tri setup work), sky tile quantization, light-fetch trim

seg4: Heretic II DOS software renderer — avg frame time (deterministic harness)

description: Light multiply via 128KB exact LUT: REGRESSED +8.8ms world (121.8->130.6). On DOSBox, 3 extra byte loads + index math + init-check per pixel cost more than the 3 IMUL+add+shr+clamp chains they replaced. Memory is NOT cheaper than ALU in this emulator.

Texture row via __builtin_ctz shift instead of *width: REGRESSED +4.2ms world (121.8->125.98 instrumented). x86 shl-by-cl needs the count in CL, adding per-pixel register shuffling; also showed the LUT was the bigger half (130.6 combined - 126.0 shift-only).

asi.next_lever: structural: tile-coarse z overdraw culling; sky tiles; present-path; entity sheet

description: Custom RGBA32->XRGB8888 per-pixel shuffle in SW_Present replaced SDL_ConvertPixels: REGRESSED present 23,172->28,737us (+24%). SDL's built-in converter beats a naive C loop under DJGPP on DOSBox. Reverted.

asi.mechanism: present path hand shuffle vs SDL_ConvertPixels
asi.next_action_hint: sky flat-tile tagging; or row-major sw_color so present converts the same rows the renderer writes (cache-local, no effect on DOSBox though). Skip more present micro-opts.

description: Measurement-only commit: entity-pass split timers (bench_us_ent_flex/sprite + model counters) and guest SWREAL.OUT publishing. No perf claim (frame 193,396 vs prior discard run 193,332 = within noise). Baseline-equivalent; keeps anatomy scaffolding for the next swing.

asi.learning: entity pass 36.9ms = flex 20.8ms + sprites 0.014ms + ~16ms inline-face gap attributed in world timers. Flex pixel work tiny (~1038 px/frame) so ~20ms sits in per-model/tri setup. Next: sub-stage flex timers.

description: Measurement-only: full entity-pass anatomy. entities 41.8ms(inflated by uclock pairs in tri loop; real ~36.9) = flex 25.6ms + brush 14.8ms + sprites 0.014. Flex tris: 320/frame, 45% bbox-culled already, 0 behind-camera; dispatch ~70% of tri cost. Brush: 175 inline faces/frame via draw_face with full float setup ~85us each. Gates PASS; frame 198,278 same-within-noise as instrumentation equivalents.

asi.learning: Entities fully decomposed. uclock ~10us/call on DOSBox => keep <=2 pairs per hot loop. x87 emulation tax (~10-30cy/op) is the per-primitive flattener for flex gradients + brush draw_face float setup.
asi.next_action_hint: Next swings: (1) cheap screen-bbox early-out in entity brush loop before draw_face (count zero-px faces first); (2) early bbox test in flex mesh loop before colors/corner-fill for the 45% culled; (3) fixed-point flex edge stepping/span-start if FPU tax confirms.

description: Hygiene+micro: removed per-tri uclock pairs (~5ms measurement tax), hoisted flex bbox/behind trivial-reject before colors/corner fill for the 45% offscreen tris (pixel-identical). True cull gain only ~0.1ms (proj lookup dominates culled-tri cost). Vs equal-instrumentation run: entities 36,890->36,770us. Gates PASS.

asi.learning: uclock pairs cost ~3us each in loop contexts (5ms/frame for 320 tri-loop pairs). Early bbox cull saves little because flex_proj_lookup itself is the culled-tri cost center.
asi.next_action_hint: brush entity faces: 14.8ms/frame over 175 draw_face calls (85us each, full float setup, no per-face cull before call). Measure zero-pixel face share, then bbox-cull entity models at the model level before the face loop (model bounds -> screen bbox), which skips all 175 draw_face calls when offscreen.

description: Whole-model bounding-sphere frustum cull for brush/inline entities (rotation-safe, pixel-exact cone half-spaces). Only 42 of ~380 model-drops/frame culled => entities 36,770->36,349us (-1.2%), brush timer 14,789->14,363us. The 85us/face cost is in ON-screen draw_face setup, not offscreen waste. Gates PASS.

asi.learning: Brush entity waste is NOT offscreen models (only ~10% culled). It is per-face full-setup (clip/project/gradients/light-fetch, all float x87) for small inline-model faces. 175 faces/frame x ~85us.
asi.next_action_hint: Per-face screen-bbox early-out inside draw_face BEFORE gradient/light setup, sharing the same cone half-space test on the face's projected polygon; or face-cluster the inline model's faces by screen tile once per frame

description: Depth buffer -> uint32 float-bit keys (exact: all depths non-negative, bits order as int). Per-block int key endpoints + int stepping replaces per-pixel FADD+FCOM in world/flex span loops. frame 192,857->192,699us = WITHIN NOISE (-0.08%). Gates PASS (z-tie linearization inside documented budget). Kept as infrastructure for int-domain coarse-z tile reject. MAJOR LEARNING: x87-tax theory REFUTED - DOSBox soft-fpu ops are cheap host-side; per-px cost is instruction-count dominated, not FPU dominated. All FPU-avoidance mechanisms (flex fixed-point) mis-ranked.

asi.learning: FPU avoidance buys ~nothing under DOSBox (host soft-float). 92-120cy/px world cost = raw instruction count. Future wins must cut instructions/branches per px or skip px wholesale.
asi.next_action_hint: Measure world z pass-ratio (depth_writes vs walked px) to size coarse 8x8-tile z-reject before building it

description: Sky-after-world: SW_RasterSky runs after SW_RasterWorld and writes only px whose depth-key is still 0 (far). Sky writes no depth so entities/lights/blend unchanged. Frame 192,699->171,307us (-11.1%), sky 38,182->16,831 (-56%). Gates PASS - trans-over-sky blend-order change is within pixel budget in bench scene. LEARNING CONFIRMS instruction-count model: ~56% of sky px were world-covered; each now costs one int compare.

asi.learning: Sky was rendering full 76.8K-px viewport with ~56% later overwritten by world. Pass-order + far-depth gate kills the overdraw wholesale. Same trick family (skip covered px wholesale, not per-px micro-ops) is what moved the needle.
asi.next_action_hint: World pass last-resort structural: 92-120cy/px * 108K px. Consider span-block height=2 pairing or runs-on-light texel re-fetch suppression; entities: flex per-tri instruction-count audit (gradient SW_GRADIENT x5 + edge funcs in float)
